key_insight: ProofLoom turns proof obligations into a control signal for building Lean theories and models without changing the target mathematical claim.
engineering_relevance: The system offers a scalable workflow for autoformalizing stochastic optimization papers by coupling model construction, theorem planning, and proof auditing with reusable verified libraries.
method: Starts from a published algorithm, target theorem, and source proof, then autonomously builds the Lean model and supporting theory.
Uses signature contracts, a Judge, Planner, and Audit to track obligations, reject unsupported assumptions, and verify the proof path.
Accumulates reusable verified lemmas and records failed modeling/proof routes for later tasks.
evidence_signal: On 15 tasks, ProofLoom achieved mean human ratings of 6.3/7 and 6.4/7, outperforming the strongest baseline by about 1.3 points, and produced 490,693 lines of Lean code with no sorry across 33 developments.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on careful proof-obligation management and model revisions, its reliability may still hinge on the quality of retrieved theory, auditing, and task-specific mathematical assumptions.
paper_title: ProofLoom: Proof-Obligation-Driven Theory Construction for Autoformalizing Research-Level Stochastic Optimization
